_comment: Feed Fork C routing registry — the map from 'what a doc is' to 'where it goes'. Data, not code. Rules match SOLELY on doc_type (the AI's classification). Rows walked top-down; first match wins; 'ledger' is ALWAYS appended by the router. NOTE_KEYWORDS REMOVED 2026-07-18: they were inert (the router is never handed the submitter's note) AND unsafe — R-analytics routes to planetiq (an external write), and a free-text note containing 'spend'/'kpi' could have overridden the real doc_type and mis-routed any document externally. All six rules already have distinct doc_types, so doc_type matching does the whole job. If notes should ever influence routing, that is a deliberate redesign (tie-breaker only, never override, never route external), built when a real document proves the need. Adding a route = adding a rule here. Later phase promotes this file to a Google Sheet.

rules._note: Consolidated vendor bills (UPS weekly, utilities, ad spend) cover MANY jobs, so they have no single job by design — they belong to a PERIOD. Holly's ruling 2026-07-16, proven on a real UPS invoice. period_expense and expense are DISTINCT doc_types (no overlap), so order is not load-bearing now that note keywords are gone — but kept ABOVE R-expense as a cheap seatbelt.
Job-attributable one-off expense (a single freight charge billed to one job). Job stays optional; use R-period-expense for consolidated bills.
